Preserve the supplied starting frame's exact buyer, glasses, hair, light facial hair, steel-blue overshirt, dark navy tee, diffuse daylight, room and table geometry. Preserve this front/three-quarter, off-center view: buyer right of center, both glasses lenses visible, owner softly in the left foreground. Keep the same side of the conversational action line. No zoom, pan, camera orbit, reframing or cuts.

Over the next second his eyes lower toward the existing table, with only a small natural follow of the head. Keep his face in the same front/three-quarter view, never turning into profile. For the remaining four seconds he quietly holds the lowered gaze with normal breathing and an ordinary blink. He is considering what he has heard; leave his thought unresolved. Do not add a verdict, suspicion, a knowing smile, anger or theatrical worry. No speaking, lip flapping, new question, nod, head shake, glance into the lens or return to speaking. Keep hands naturally where the starting frame places them. No new writing, phone, document, prop, person or action. The owner remains a quiet foreground presence. Real-time restrained motion; no captions, logos or generated sound.
